name: U.S. Department of the Treasury — Interest Rate Statistics
description: The Treasury Department's own interest-rate data center: daily par yield curve rates (nominal Constant Maturity Treasury) and daily par real yield curve rates (TIPS-derived Real CMT), each served as one CSV per calendar year, plus the High Quality Market (HQM) corporate bond yield curve used for pension discounting, published as downloadable Excel workbooks.

notes: type is daily_treasury_yield_curve for nominal or daily_treasury_real_yield_curve for real; {year} is the four-digit calendar year.

The current-year file is server-cached: a plain request returns Drupal cache header X-Drupal-Cache: HIT, and adding an unrecognized query parameter (e.g. &junk=1) returns X-Drupal-Cache: MISS. Verified by comparing response headers on 2026-09-15 for the 2026 nominal file; on that check the cached and freshly-generated copies held identical data (latest row was already the newest business day), so this confirms the cache exists, not that it ever serves a stale current-year file. A fetcher pulling same-day data should still add a cache-busting parameter as a precaution.
Prior-year files (type={dataset}, {year} < current year) are static once the year closes and are not known to have this caching behavior.

terms.summary: U.S. federal government work; Treasury's site policies state no copyright may be claimed for federal-employee work and that images and text on the site may be freely copied, with a caveat that some third-party material embedded on the site may carry its own copyright.

datasets.name: Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates (nominal CMTs)
datasets.gives: Par (Constant Maturity Treasury) yields read off Treasury's daily nominal yield curve, at maturities that have grown from 9 tenors in 1990 to 14 today (1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6 months; 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 30 years), computed from over-the-counter closing bid quotations compiled by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York
notes: Verified the 1990-01-02 start directly: the 1990 CSV returns data (last row 12/31/1990) while the 1989 CSV returns an empty body (header row only, no data rows).

1990 file carries only 9 tenors (3mo, 6mo, 1yr, 2yr, 3yr, 5yr, 7yr, 10yr, 30yr); the 2026 file carries 14 (1mo, 1.5mo, 2mo, 3mo, 4mo, 6mo, 1yr, 2yr, 3yr, 5yr, 7yr, 10yr, 20yr, 30yr) — Treasury has added tenors over time (e.g. 1-month in 2001, 20-year resumed in 2020, 1.5-month/2-month/4-month added later); which tenor appears in which year was not fully mapped, only the 1990 and 2026 endpoints checked.
Publication lag observed as same business day: the CSV requested 2026-09-15 already carried the 09/14/2026 row as its latest observation.
Same underlying data as FRED's DGS* constant-maturity series (catalog/sources/fred.json), fetched here directly from Treasury instead of via FRED.

datasets.name: Daily Treasury Par Real Yield Curve Rates (Real CMTs / R-CMTs)
datasets.gives: Par real yields (TIPS-derived) read off Treasury's daily real yield curve at 5 maturities (5, 7, 10, 20, 30 years), interpolated with a monotone convex spline from indicative secondary-market TIPS quotations compiled by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York
notes: Verified the 2003-01-02 start directly: the 2003 CSV returns data (last row 12/31/2003, only 5yr/7yr/10yr present that year) while the 2002 CSV returns an empty body.
2003 file carries only 3 tenors (5yr, 7yr, 10yr); the 2026 file carries all 5 (5yr, 7yr, 10yr, 20yr, 30yr) — 20-year and 30-year were added later, exact addition year not checked.
Publication lag observed as same business day: the CSV requested 2026-09-15 already carried the 09/14/2026 row as its latest observation.
Shares the same current-year caching behavior noted in access.notes (checked against the nominal file, not independently reverified for this dataset).

datasets.name: HQM Corporate Bond Yield Curve, par yields
datasets.gives: Par yields on the High Quality Market (HQM) corporate bond yield curve (AAA/AA/A-rated corporates), used for Pension Protection Act discounting; a single workbook spanning 1984 to present, plus a separate end-of-month-only workbook
notes: Treasury also publishes HQM spot rates (not par yields) as separate .xls workbooks chunked into 5-year windows (e.g. hqm_84_88.xls ... hqm_24_28.xls, plus end-of-month equivalents hqmeom_84_88.xls ...); not catalogued as a separate dataset here since we don't use spot rates.

A related but distinct HQM series (HQMCB1YR-HQMCB30YR, spot rates, monthly, from 1984) is catalogued as dataset hqmcb in catalog/sources/fred.json; that is a spot-rate curve, not par yields, and is the dataset series_meta.py resolves today (confirmed against FRED's HQMCB10YR series page: 'This series represents a spot rate, not a par yield... The spot rate for any maturity is defined as the yield on a bond that gives a single payment at that maturity.'). This entry records Treasury's own par-yield workbooks as the direct, non-FRED alternative.

File format read from filenames and link titles only (page is heavily JavaScript-instrumented; no page prose describing update frequency was found near the hqm_qh_pars.xls link, reconfirmed 2026-09-15), so both cadence and publication_lag_business_days are unknown rather than guessed.

General U.S. federal-government-work public-domain status likely applies but was not confirmed with a verbatim quote from this specific Treasury page.
